# `Q-12-4` — Listing Id Collision

> Two or more listings on the same page declare the same `id`;
> later occurrences are dropped.

## What this means

Every listing on a page gets an `id`: either one the author set
explicitly, or one Quarto assigned — `listing` for a page's only
listing, `listing-1`, `listing-2`, ... for the entries of a
`listing:` array. The id names the `::: {#id}` div a listing renders
into, and the rendered listing's HTML element is `listing-<id>`
(`#listing-listing` for the default), which CSS and anchor links
target. The parser requires the ids on a page to be unique.

When two listings on the same page share an id, the first one
keeps it and any later listings with the same id are dropped
entirely.

## Why this happens

A `listing:` array in front matter has two entries that explicitly
set `id:` to the same string. (Assigned ids never collide: Quarto
skips any `listing-N` an entry has already claimed explicitly.)

## How to fix

Pick distinct ids. If you do not need a specific id for either
listing, remove the `id:` field from both and let Quarto assign
unique defaults.
